name: Quality Control
tagline: Analytical QC, GMP compliance, and pharmaceutical quality assurance.
seo_title: Quality Control — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Quality Control on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in pharmaceutical QC, analytical validation, GMP and data integrity.

definition.lead: Quality control checks that every batch of a product meets its specifications, so that what reaches the customer, or the patient, is exactly what the label says.
definition.body: In chemical and pharmaceutical plants it combines validated analytical methods, sampling plans, statistics and careful documentation. Its rules, Good Manufacturing Practice, exist because past failures harmed people.

facts.label: Walter Shewhart invents the control chart
US Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, passed after the elixir sulfanilamide deaths
typical control limits on a Shewhart chart

branches.name: Analytical testing
branches.summary: Identity, assay, purity and impurities of every batch.
branches.example: HPLC assay of the active ingredient.

branches.name: Method validation
branches.summary: Proving that a test method is fit for purpose.

branches.name: Statistical process control
branches.summary: Using statistics to spot drift before it causes failure.

branches.name: Good Manufacturing Practice
branches.summary: The rules for making medicines consistently.
branches.example: If it isn't documented, it didn't happen.

branches.name: Stability testing
branches.summary: How a product changes over time.
branches.example: Setting shelf life and storage conditions.

branches.name: Microbiological control
branches.summary: Keeping products free of harmful microbes.

branches.name: Quality by design
branches.summary: Building quality in from development, not testing it in at the end.
branches.example: Defining a design space for a process.

branches.name: Data integrity
branches.summary: Making sure records are complete, original and trustworthy.

timeline.title: Pure Food and Drug Act
timeline.text: The United States passes its first federal food and drug law.

timeline.title: The control chart
timeline.text: Walter Shewhart sketches the first control chart at Bell Labs.
timeline.why: The birth of statistical quality control.

timeline.title: Proof of safety
timeline.text: After more than 100 deaths from a toxic drug solvent, the US requires safety evidence before sale.

timeline.title: After thalidomide
timeline.text: The Kefauver–Harris amendments require proof of effectiveness as well as safety.

timeline.title: GMP rules
timeline.text: The US issues its first Good Manufacturing Practice regulations for drugs.
timeline.why: Quality became a legal requirement in manufacturing.

timeline.title: ISO 9000
timeline.text: The first ISO 9000 quality management standards are published.
timeline.why: A shared language for quality across industries.

timeline.title: ICH
timeline.text: Regulators and industry from Europe, Japan and the US create the ICH.

timeline.title: Modernizing GMP
timeline.text: The FDA promotes process analytical technology and risk-based GMP.
timeline.why: Real-time monitoring instead of only end testing.

timeline.title: Quality by design
timeline.text: ICH Q8 on pharmaceutical development is adopted.
timeline.why: Process understanding became central to quality.

quiz.q: What is the difference between QC and QA?
options: QC tests products; QA designs the systems that ensure quality
QA tests products; QC designs systems
quiz.explain: QC finds problems; QA prevents them.

quiz.q: What is a control chart for?
options: Spotting when a process drifts beyond its normal variation
Counting how many staff work each shift
Measuring the profit of each production batch
quiz.explain: Points outside the limits signal something has changed.

quiz.q: Typical control limits are set at…
options: The lowest and highest values ever seen
quiz.explain: A stable process rarely produces points beyond ±3σ by chance.
Rules covering people, premises, equipment, documents and processes.

options: Measures the analyte without interference from other components
Is fast enough for routine testing
Is cheap enough for every batch
Measures everything in the sample at once
quiz.explain: Impurities and excipients must not distort the result.
Samples are stored under defined temperature and humidity and tested over time.

options: A documented investigation before any conclusion
quiz.explain: 'Testing into compliance' is a serious violation.

quiz.q: In data integrity, ALCOA stands for…
quiz.explain: Records must show who did what, when, in the original form.

quiz.q: What did the 1962 Kefauver–Harris amendments add after thalidomide?
options: Proof that a drug works, as well as that it is safe
A ban on all new drugs for ten years
The end of Good Manufacturing Practice rules
Nothing new; they repeated earlier rules
quiz.explain: Thalidomide caused severe birth defects in thousands of children.
Deming later spread Shewhart's ideas worldwide.

options: A document reporting a batch's test results against its specifications
An invoice sent with each delivery to the customer
A patent covering the product's formula
Only the safety data sheet for the product
quiz.explain: It travels with the batch to the customer.

options: Understanding how process parameters affect quality and building it in from development
Testing many more samples at the end of production
quiz.explain: Quality cannot be tested into a product; it must be designed in.
